overview: White plays f4 at once, taking space and building an Austrian Attack-style centre; Black usually plays 2...Nf6 3.Nc3 g6 4.Nf3 Bg7, reaching a Pirc with f4 already played. White aims for e5 and a kingside attack with Bc4 and O-O, while Black counterattacks the centre with ...c5 or ...e5. Positions are imbalanced with White's space against Black's flank counterplay.

white_ideas.idea: Use f4 and e4 with Nf3, Bc4 and castle for a kingside attack or e5 space gain
Take a broad centre with d4 and push e5 to cramp Black

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the bishop on g7 and undermine the centre with ...c5 or ...e5
Strike at the overextended f4/e4 pawns with ...c5 and ...Nc6, or ...d5

typical_structures.structure: Austrian-style Pirc: White e4/f4 centre against ...d6/g6 fianchetto

character.notes: Austrian-style centre invites mutual attacks and sharp tactics; imbalanced.

structure.notes: The e4/f4 centre against a ...d6 fianchetto; may be attacked or locked; undecided.

approach.notes: A recognised line against the Pirc and played by strong players; less common than 2.d4.

level.notes: Plans are clear for White, but Black needs accurate timing of ...c5 or ...e5.

sublines_that_differ.name: Quiet 2.f4 lines
sublines_that_differ.moves: 2. f4 Nf6 3. Nc3 g6 4. Nf3 Bg7 5. Bc4 O-O 6. O-O Nc6 7. d3
sublines_that_differ.how: White skips d4 and plays a slower game with d3.

character.reason: White's Austrian-style set-up means mutual attacks and one-move errors.

structure.reason: The e4/f4 centre faces breaks and is not yet fixed.

approach.reason: A recognised line in the Pirc family.

level.reason: Needs a feel for Austrian Attack plans but not a long tree.

plans.reason: White's f4 and e4 aim at space and an attack on the king.
